new.n: Dig spot: James Murphy's missing ~$24,000, Murphy farm barnyard, Warsaw Twp (Rice Co.)
new.pl: James Murphy farmstead, E half of SE quarter of sec. 23 T109N R21W (Warsaw township), Rice County; about 80 m W of Bagley Ave
new.v: About $24,000 in gold coin (1902 value), unfound
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: About $24,000 in gold that James Murphy kept hidden about the house was never found; only one crock ($6,000) turned up, in 1920, under a rotten board in the barnyard by the cow barn. His only farmstead (1900 plat dot, 1938 air photo) is gone and farmed over, but 2021 LiDAR still shows the building pads and a pit. Work the house pad first, then the barnyard edge: the 1920 crock lay just outside the old barnyard.
new.t: Private cropland: ask the owner; best after harvest. Search radius about 75 m around the pin. Lead grade B; the full story, every source and the pin evidence are on the lead card.

new.n: Dig spot: Vejvoda's buried silver, farm NE of Rice Lake
new.pl: Vejvoda 80 acres, S½ SE¼ sec. 23 T36N R11W, Town of Bear Lake (Barron Co.), farmstead dot near the SE corner (Hixson plat book, about 1915)
new.v: About $6,000 recovered; "a large quantity of silver" said to be buried between the road and the house
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: After his wife died in 1925 John Vejvoda dug up about $6,000 she had hidden, and said there was 'a large quantity of silver buried between the road and the house'. No later find was reported. The 1939 air photo shows the only farmstead on the Vejvoda 80, about 60 m north of the south road. The strip between that road and the house site is the story's own spot: grid it slowly, silver reads lower than gold.

new.n: Dig spot: Danish recluse Lars Nielson's $10,000-13,000 hidden on his farm, sec 14 Morken Township
new.pl: Nielson farm, W half of sec 14 T141N R47W, Morken Twp (Clay Co.)
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: Lars Nielson never used a bank and left $10,000-13,000 in gold, silver and currency that nobody found; the administrator's search and night diggers in 1919 came up empty. His sod shanty stood 32 years and was thought the likeliest spot; the 1909 plat dot and the 1939 farmstead are both inside this ring on his homestead quarter (GLO patent 1885). The later house had no cellar.

new.n: Dig spot: The Bronson "gold farm": $3,000 in gold dug up, one plugged tile still missing
new.pl: About 4 mi W of Bronson: sec. 5 T7S R8W, Bronson Twp (1894 Branch County atlas parcel; the Battle Creek Enquirer's "2 mi east" looks like an error). 1915 atlas: same family estate, house at N end of the strip by the township-line road.
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: In 1939 boys dug up a drain tile with $1,880 in gold and a pipe with $1,120 turned up 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, was played with and then lost; it was never found again. The caches were in the house yard of the family strip in the N half of sec. 5 (1894 and 1915 atlases); the house stood at the N end by the township-line road. Search that yard: a concrete-plugged tile or iron pipe reads as a strong iron or mixed target.
new.t: Private farm: ask the owner. Search radius about 450 m around the pin. Lead grade B; the full story, every source and the pin evidence are on the lead card.

new.n: Dig spot: Noah Keeler's missing $7,000, Liberty Township
new.pl: Keeler farm, house dots on the west edge of the NW quarter of sec. 14 T4S R1W, Liberty Township, about 8 mi S of Jackson (1874 Jackson County atlas)
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: Noah Keeler, who once hid gold in a sack of beans, died in 1892 and about $7,000 he left could not be found; his estate's final account (1894) reports no find. He lived on this farm from 1840 to 1892: the 1874 atlas house dots on the west edge of the NW quarter of sec. 14 are the target, with the old farmyard around them.

new.n: Dig spot: Fred Noyes' buried gold, his former farm in Eden Township near Scottville
new.pl: Noyes 80 acres, SW¼ NW¼ sec. 5 and SE¼ NE¼ sec. 6 T17N R16W (Eden Twp), near Scottville; house mark at the NW corner of the sec. 5 forty on the 5/6 line, about 0.3 mi S of the Custer Twp line (1904 Standard Atlas of Mason County)
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: In 1935 Fred Noyes said gold he buried about 30 years earlier was still on his family's old farm ($25,000 to $85,000 in different wire copies). He had lost his map and a day's dig with a federal agent failed. The 1904 atlas puts the Noyes 80 here with the house mark at the NW corner of the sec. 5 forty. His landmarks were the rail fence and the house: find the old house site and fence lines on the 1938 air photo, then search out from them.

new.n: Dig spot: The poisoned Englishman Carr's California gold, orchard farm east of Dimondale
new.pl: Orchard farm on a side hill 4 mi E of Dimondale: a 40 on the 1895 Ingham County atlas (Delhi Twp), NE¼ NE¼ sec. 30 T3N R2W, house mark at the E edge of the forty on the 29/30 line road. 1874 atlas: no 1850-era owner confirmed on the plate.
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: In 1895 a man dragging an orchard side hill here turned up a box of gold nuggets and flakes; the story says the dying Englishman Carr buried 'this gold with other nuggets and money in this neighborhood'. The 1895 atlas house mark on the E edge of the forty (sec. 30, Delhi Twp) with the side-hill orchard ground around it. The rest is legend: treat it as a long shot on a proven find spot.
new.t: The pin parcel is township land (Delhi Charter Township, 2025 parcel map): ask the township before detecting there; the farms around it are private. Search radius about 200 m around the pin. Lead grade B; the full story, every source and the pin evidence are on the lead card.

new.n: Dig spot: F. Marion Ogle's hidden gold, shanty-and-dugout farm near Medora
new.pl: Centre of sec. 9 T74N R24W, the heart of the 1940 Ogle family land just east of Medora, Warren County
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: F. Marion Ogle hid gold about his shanty-and-dugout farm; days before his fatal accident in 1907 he banked $10,000 of it, and people believed more was still hidden. The 1902 Warren County atlas shows his 80 acres with a house dot; the pin is on that house. Look for the dugout's hollow and the shanty site near it.

new.n: Dig spot: Patrick Mulchrone's hidden money, west of Liberty Pole
new.pl: Patrick Mulchrone's farm, sec. 2 T11N R5W, town of Franklin, about 3 mi W of Liberty Pole; the 1896 Vernon County plat shows his 113-acre farm with a building dot, with the Zitzner (Fitzner) 160 adjoining in the same section
new.v: "Several hundred if not thousands of dollars" believed hidden on the premises
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade B lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: Patrick Mulchrone was murdered in 1899 and was believed to have hundreds or thousands of dollars hidden about his place. In 1900 a gang tore out the old homestead's foundation looking for it; no find was reported. The 1896 plat building dot on his 113 acres, close to the Zitzner farm as the 1899 paper says. The dug-out foundation should still show as a hollow with a spoil bank: search the yard, outbuildings and lane around it, not the hole they already dug.
new.t: Private farm: ask the owner. Search radius about 450 m around the pin. Lead grade B; the full story, every source and the pin evidence are on the lead card.

new.n: Dig spot: Michael Zopp's hidden money, Trimbelle (1912)
new.tovw: Dig spot on a grade C lead (placed farm, cache not recovered): see the lead card
new.st: Why here: Blacksmith Michael Zopp died in May 1912 without telling where he had hidden his savings (several thousand dollars, up to $20,000 in some reports). Relatives dug on his farm that June without success. The pin is in the S½ NE¼ sec. 30 T26N R18W (checked on the BLM section grid), the 80 that the 1909 Ogle atlas marks 'MICHL ZOPP 80' with a house mark and the c.1915 plat marks 'Mich'l Zopp 80 Est.': the farm he held when he died. Start at the house mark.
new.t: Private farm: ask the owner. Search radius about 200 m around the pin. Lead grade C; the full story, every source and the pin evidence are on the lead card.
